title: Suspense Resource Promise Wrapper (wrapPromise)
concept: Suspense Protocol: Throwing Promises on Pending State
problemStatement: Implement `wrapPromise(promise)` that returns an object with a `read()` method. If the promise is pending, `read()` MUST throw the promise itself. If rejected, it throws the error. If resolved, it returns the resolved data.
interviewTrap: Throwing a promise is how React Suspense detects async loading. If wrapPromise is instantiated inside the render body instead of cached, a new Promise is created on every render, locking the UI in an infinite suspension loop.

testCases.name: Throws the suspender promise while pending
testCases.input: resource.read() on pending promise throws Promise
testCases.testFn: const p = new Promise(() => {}); const resource = wrapPromise(p); try { resource.read(); return false; } catch (thrown) { return thrown instanceof Promise; }

testCases.name: Returns data synchronously once resolved
testCases.testFn: const p = Promise.resolve('DataLoaded'); const resource = wrapPromise(p); return p.then(() => resource.read());

testCases.name: Throws error when rejected
testCases.testFn: const p = Promise.reject(new Error('NetworkFail')); const resource = wrapPromise(p); return p.catch(() => {}).then(() => { try { resource.read(); return false; } catch (e) { return e.message; } });

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: When a component suspends, it throws a Promise up the Fiber tree. React catches the promise, pauses the render phase for that branch, renders the nearest Suspense fallback, and resumes when the promise resolves.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Suspense Protocol: Throwing Promises on Pending State.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
